---
title: "Changing conditional variance"
execute:
  enabled: true
  echo: true
  warning: false
  message: false
---

Ordinary linear regression assumes one conditional residual variance. **Heteroscedasticity** means that this spread changes across observations, as formalized below.

Recall that a [residual](residuals.qmd) is observed minus fitted response. Its conditional [variance and standard deviation](../random-variables-and-distributions/variance-and-covariance.qmd) concern response spread, while a coefficient [standard error](../statistical-inference/standard-errors.qmd) concerns estimator variation; covariance among coefficient estimates records their joint uncertainty. For MALD item means, unequal retained-trial counts can change precision, and onset timing complicates an acoustic-duration interpretation.

The empirical question is whether MALD item summaries have the same remaining spread across frequency. Robust covariance and distributional regression respond to a failure in different places, one in coefficient uncertainty and the other in the response model.

$$
\operatorname{Var}[Y_i\mid\mathbf x_i]=\sigma_i^2
$$

rather than

$$
\operatorname{Var}[Y_i\mid\mathbf x_i]=\sigma^2.
$$

## Residual spread across MALD frequency

The MALD regression provides two related spread measurements: absolute residuals from the item-mean model and the stored within-item standard deviation of correct log response times.

They are different random objects. The item-mean residual

$$
e_i=\overline y_i-\widehat\mu_i
$$

compares one word's aggregated mean with the between item regression. The stored $s_i$ summarizes variation among retained correct trials within that word. Between item model misspecification can enlarge $|e_i|$ even when within item spread is stable, and participant heterogeneity can enlarge $s_i$ even when the item mean equation is adequate. The [MALD data discussion](multiple-regression.qmd#mald-word-item-data) explains the aggregation that separates these levels.

```{r}
#| label: compute-mald-heteroscedasticity
library(ggplot2)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

mald <- read.csv("data/mald/mald-items.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
mald$log_frequency_c <-
  mald$log_frequency_subtlex - mean(mald$log_frequency_subtlex)
mald$log_duration_c <- mald$log_duration - mean(mald$log_duration)
mald$n_phones_c <- mald$n_phones - mean(mald$n_phones)

fit <- lm(
  mean_log_rt ~ log_frequency_c + log_duration_c + n_phones_c,
  data = mald
)
mald$residual <- residuals(fit)

breaks <- unique(quantile(
  mald$log_frequency_subtlex,
  probs = seq(0, 1, length.out = 11L)
))
mald$frequency_bin <- cut(
  mald$log_frequency_subtlex,
  breaks = breaks,
  include.lowest = TRUE
)
spread_bins <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(mald, mald$frequency_bin),
  function(rows) data.frame(
    mean_log_frequency = mean(rows$log_frequency_subtlex),
    mean_absolute_residual = mean(abs(rows$residual)),
    mean_within_item_sd = mean(rows$sd_log_rt),
    n_items = nrow(rows)
  )
))
row.names(spread_bins) <- NULL

conventional_se <- coef(summary(fit))[, "Std. Error"]
hc3_test <- coeftest(fit, vcov. = vcovHC(fit, type = "HC3"))
hc3_se <- hc3_test[, "Std. Error"]

data.frame(
  term = names(coef(fit)),
  conventional_se = conventional_se,
  hc3_se = hc3_se,
  ratio = hc3_se / conventional_se
)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-mald-heteroscedasticity
#| fig-cap: "Absolute MALD residuals with equal-count-bin means in blue."
point_opacity <- 0.045
ggplot(mald, aes(log_frequency_subtlex, abs(residual))) +
  geom_point(color = "grey70", alpha = point_opacity, size = 0.5) +
  geom_line(
    data = spread_bins,
    aes(mean_log_frequency, mean_absolute_residual),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#2C6E9B",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = spread_bins,
    aes(mean_log_frequency, mean_absolute_residual),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#2C6E9B",
    size = 1.5
  ) +
  labs(x = "Log SUBTLEX frequency", y = "Absolute residual") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

```{r}
#| label: plot-mald-within-item-spread
#| fig-cap: "Observed within-item log-response-time standard deviations and their equal-count-bin means."
ggplot(mald, aes(log_frequency_subtlex, sd_log_rt)) +
  geom_point(color = "grey70", alpha = point_opacity, size = 0.5) +
  geom_line(
    data = spread_bins,
    aes(mean_log_frequency, mean_within_item_sd),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#2C6E9B",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(x = "Log SUBTLEX frequency", y = "Within-item log-RT SD") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

HC3 changes the covariance estimate while preserving the OLS coefficients and fitted means. It is a sensitivity analysis for coefficient uncertainty, not a model of why spread changes. The next page instead gives conditional scale its own regression equation.

HC0 replaces the homoscedastic middle of the sandwich covariance by squared row residuals. HC3 further divides residual $e_i$ by $1-h_{ii}$ before squaring, which increases the contribution of high-leverage observations whose ordinary residuals tend to be compressed by fitting. This is a covariance repair. It does not make the variance constant, supply a probability model for $\sigma_i$, or recover participant dependence.

The within-item spread is computed across retained correct trials. Because the item table lacks participant identifiers, neither plot separates participant heterogeneity from residual trial variation.

## Recap and check your understanding

1. Which ordinary regression assumption does heteroscedasticity violate?
2. Why do robust standard errors leave fitted means unchanged?
3. What does `sd_log_rt` summarize?
4. Which source of dependence remains unavailable?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Heteroscedasticity violates the ordinary regression assumption that $\operatorname{Var}[Y_i\mid\mathbf x_i]=\sigma^2$ is constant across observations. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. Robust standard errors replace the coefficient covariance estimate after OLS minimizes the same SSE, so the coefficients and fitted means remain unchanged. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. `sd_log_rt` summarizes the standard deviation of retained correct log response times within each MALD word item. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. Participant-level dependence and participant heterogeneity remain unavailable because the item table omits participant identifiers. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>

The [next page](distributional-regression.qmd) models frequency-dependent scale directly.
